cultural_entities.translation_note: Translated literally as 'black waters' or 'black water'. While literally meaning dark water, in South Asian history it specifically refers to the Cellular Jail in the Andaman Islands and the sentence of exile across the ocean, carrying deep connotations of colonial imprisonment, isolation, and struggle.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The historical and cultural resonance of 'Kaala Paani' (काला पानी), which refers specifically to the colonial-era penal settlement in the Andaman Islands (literally 'black water' or 'dark water' representing exile and inescapable punishment), is flattened into the literal translation 'black waters'.

The translation of 'अपनी यात्रा' (apni yaatra) as 'our journey' shifts the possessive pronoun 'apni' (which is reflexive and typically means 'one's own' or 'my own' depending on context) to a collective 'our', altering the individualistic tone of the personal struggle.

The translation of 'समझ के साथ' (with understanding) as 'Understanding' in the phrase 'Understanding the silence of hunger' changes the grammatical structure from a prepositional phrase of accompaniment/manner to a participle modifying the action, which slightly alters the relationship between 'understanding' and 'the silence of hunger'.

annotation.theme: Overcoming the psychological and physical confinement of 'Kaala Paani' through inner resolve, endurance, and calm determination.

original_poem:
काला पानी, काला पानी, ये काला पानी है,
कहाँ तक भागोगे तुम, कहां तक डरोगे तुम?
है विश्वास, तो यही संकल्प हो सका,
तब, एक दिन, काला पानी मिटा सकते हो तुम।
किसी के बिना, किसी के साथ, समंदर के किनारे
समझ के साथ, भूख की चुप्पी, शिकंजे की आँखों को चुराकर।
समझ लो, यह काला पानी अपनी यात्रा है,
जितना शीतल होगा, उतना दूर चल पाओगे तुम।
translated_poem:
The black waters, the black waters, these black waters,
How long will you run, how long will you fear?
If there is belief, then this resolution can be made,
One day, you can erase these black waters.
Alone or with someone, by the shore of the ocean
Understanding the silence of hunger, sneaking past the eyes of the shackles.
Understand this, the black water is our journey,
The cooler it is, the farther you will go.
